newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 28.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents.
-- 4 BILLION STG HALIFAX STOCK ON OFFER

Halifax banking society has announced that 23 percent of its members have chosen to sell their shares in the converted building society right away, netting them about 2,300 stg each. The number of shares that would be sold is about 568 million, with a total worth of 4 billion stg. The 23 percent of available shares will be put up for auction and has been deemed a satisfactory amount to be available to pension funds and insurance companies by the society.
-- BROWN NEED NOT RAISE TAXES, SAYS IFS STUDY

A study by the Institute for Fiscal Studies says that UK chancellor Gordon Brown does not need to increase taxes in his soon to be released mini-budget. The study found that measures inherited from the Conservatives including above-inflation increases in petrol and tobacco, as well as the impact of 'fiscal drag'm would be more than enough to ensure further fiscal restraint and budget tightening are not needed.
-- INSURER ACTS AGAINST 2000 'BOMB'

UK life assurance group Legal & General has announced it will give its suppliers 21 days to accept a new standard purchase order clause providing them a guarantee that all goods shipped are free of problems caused by the 'millennium bomb'. L&G said this was only the first step in a compliance programme that also includes air conditioning, security and fire protection systems and will cost it 'tens of millions of pounds'.
-- PEP SALES SOAR IN RUSH TO BEAT TAXMAN

Figures released Tuesday by the Association of Unit Trust and Investment Funds show sales of unit trust personal equity plans hit all-time highs in April as investors raced to beat the end of the tax year and the election of a new government. The surge in late March and April followed lackluster sales in February. Between April 1-5 - the end of the tax year - fund managers sold 797 million sterling of Peps to private investors.
-- SCOTTISH ASSEMBLY 'MAY LEAD TO 10,000 MORE JOBS'

Edinburgh-based property consultants Ryden International have claimed the formation of a Scottish parliament would create 5,000 to 10,000 more office jobs in the city, requiring one million square feet of office space. Among the jobs that would be created are public relations advisers, media organisations and other related businesses. A referendum will be held this autumn in Scotland asking whether citizens want their own parliament and whether it should have tax-raising powers.
--EMI CUTS COST IN NORTH AMERICA

One of the largest music companies in the world, EMI Group, will conduct a share buy-back through the rationalisation of its North American record labels to return almost 520 million stg of capital. Through the reductions, 35 senior executives will be sacked and an undisclosed number of artists will be dropped from the label. EMI, meanwhile, recently released its figures for the financial year to March 31st, including a 3.6 percent increase in pre-tax profits to 380.5 million stg against 367.3 million the year before.
-- LONRHO TO PURSUE JCI MERGER DISCUSSIONS

UK conglomerate Lonrho has decided to keep up its talks with South African mining house JCI, although the talks are said to be 'far from resolution' due to disagreements on a price or value of assets. Lonrho has said it is still examining what financial benefits would result from the merger, but the two groups have admitted they see commercial benefits in merging the businesses. Nicholas Morrell, the chief executive of Lonrho is set to meet with Mzi Khumalo, chairman of JCI on Wednesday.
-- CASPIAN IN TALKS ON DUTCH FOOTBALL ALLIANCE

The owners of Leeds United football club, Caspian, have entered talks with top Dutch football club PSV Eindhoven, owned by electronics group Phillips, to discuss a possibile alliance that would involve swapping equity stakes and an agreement to share players. If the two clubs were to come to an agreement, it would be the first instance of an alliance between a UK and an overseas team. Chris Akers of Caspian has also conducted talks with two other Dutch clubs, Sparta Rotterdam and ADO Den Haag.
-- SCOTTISH HYDRO SELLS STAKE IN VECTOR GAS

Scottish Hydro-Electric has sold its stake in Vector Gas to Quantum Gas Management, citing the lack of profits from the group and difficulty of expansion. The move signals Scottish's departure from the general industrial and commercial gas market, though it will remain a sizeable participant, concentrating on combined, heat and power and other 'total energy solutions'.
-- FORTUNE SELLS REST OF ONSHORE OIL ASSETS

Fortune Oil, the UK-based petroleum trading, distribution and marketing group that does most of its business in China, has announced it will sell its remaining UK onshore oil production assets. East Midlands Oil and Gas, which has a book value of 860,000 stg but reported losses of 63,000 stg for 1996, and the Fu Duo liquified petroleum business, which also has reported recent disappointing results, are the businesses expected to be sold. Fortune will most likely use the profit to fund its 24.5 percent share in a Chinese aviation fuel joint venture and to expand its network of petrol stations in China.
